quest.title: Pen Pals, Book Reviews, and the Super Lucky General
quest.description: The Irodori Festival is drawing to a close, but the harbor arrival schedule shows that there is still one more ship arriving bearing guests...
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x40, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x2, Amazing Gift (Furnishing) x1

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, nice to see you again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, it's Kokomi and Gorou. So the Divine Priestess and the general of Watatsumi Island have come to take part in the Irodori Festival.

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: Yes, but we are not here representing Watatsumi Island's administration. We were invited as individuals.

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: Things are quiet in Watatsumi Island at the moment, and I wanted to buy some books. So, I decided to make the trip here.

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: Gorou was not greatly interested in the Irodori Festival. But he said if I was going to Ritou, he would join me.

dialogues.speaker: Gorou
dialogues.text: Her Excellency is traveling outside of Watatsumi Island and also meeting her pen pal today. As her general, it is my duty to ensure her safety at every turn.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Pen pal?

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: Yes. We started corresponding just recently.

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: My pen pal and I share very similar tastes in light novels, and we always have a lot of interesting thoughts to share. Of course, there are also times when we fiercely disagree.

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: Since we were both coming to the Irodori Festival this time, we decided to take the opportunity to hold a book review session, and discuss our views on various novels in more depth.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds pretty professional! Hey, since you both like novels, why don't you try writing one together? Who knows, maybe you'll shake things up on the Inazuman literary scene.

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: Hehe, that's a very interesting idea.

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: #It's almost time, {NICKNAME}. Gorou and I must go to meet my pen pal at the agreed upon location.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Kokomi, Paimon's super curious about this pen pal of yours. Can Paimon come with you? Don't worry, Paimon will just watch from a distance and won't interrupt anything.

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: Hmm, let me think... Yes, I think it should be fine for you two to come with me. Alright, let's go together.

talks.objective: Accompany Kokomi to see her pen pal
Accompany Kokomi to see her pen pal

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: This is the meeting spot.

dialogues.speaker: Gorou
dialogues.text: There's no one else around. It looks like we're early...

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: My, my, who have we here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: M—Miko!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Oh no, Paimon hadn't counted on running into Miko! She and Kokomi are on different sides, and they also believe in different gods...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Are they gonna end up... having a fight?)

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: Lady Guuji of the Grand Narukami Shrine — no wonder. I was just wondering where that air of superiority was coming from.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Hehe, if it isn't the leader of Watatsumi Island, who looks as soft as a jellyfish, but whose words sting like one, too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh oh... this is getting out of control fast...

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: Hello, nice to meet you, "Fried Tofu With All the Frills."

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: The pleasure is all mine, "Sole of the Deep."

dialogues.speaker: Miko & Kokomi
dialogues.text: Hehehehehe...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey... what's going on here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Miko is Kokomi's pen pal!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No, it can't be. Look at them, clearly they already knew each other! Does that mean...

choices.text: This so-called meeting of pen pals...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Hmm? Whatever are you talking about? I don't understand. I'm simply here for the book review session with Miss Sole of the Deep.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Let's go. The venue for this meeting is in the Kanjou Commission headquarters up there. The view is excellent, making it a perfect place to drink tea and discuss creative ideas.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Who holds a book review in the Kanjou Commission? You seriously expect anyone to believe that!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're not here to talk about shaking up the Inazuman literary scene... You're here to talk about shaking up things in Inazuma as a whole.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Hehe, Watatsumi Island will soon hold formal talks with the Shogunate on Inazuma's future development. It's essential to have an informal meeting like this one before the formal talks begin.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Right. Especially with someone outside of the Shogunate like myself, who is in a good position to test out where each party draws the lines.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: But this is just our first meeting. It's a little too early to announce it to the general public.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, okay then.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: By the way, where is your general? Didn't you say he would be joining you?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, that's right... Where did Gorou go...?

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Gorou went to buy some books for me. He won't be attending the book review.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Oh, what a pity. I was rather looking forward to seeing his fluffy ears again.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, I'd like to talk to you for a moment.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What's up?

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: I have been getting the sense that Gorou does not like having to deal with Guuji Yae, so I was initially reluctant to bring him to Ritou with me this time.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: I noticed he instinctively hid as soon as he saw her just now. However, Gorou has a strong sense of responsibility, and will feel ashamed when he next sees me.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: So, I would like to give him the task of buying some books for me to make things easier for him.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: But Gorou rarely buys anything. So as a favor for me, I'd like to ask you to accompany him.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sure, leave it to me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Kokomi, you focus on the meeting with Miko. Leave the books to us and Gorou.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Thank you. I made a list of the books I'd like to buy. Please pass it on to Gorou.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Gorou, are you alright?

dialogues.speaker: Gorou
dialogues.text: Ah! It's you... *sigh* I wasn't expecting you-know-who to show up — it completely caught me by surprise. I had no idea what to say to her... Next thing I knew, I'd apparently already taken cover.

dialogues.speaker: Gorou
dialogues.text: I came here to ensure the safety of Her Excellency, but now I'm useless... I've become a burden instead.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Gorou, don't be so hard on yourself. Actually, Kokomi asked us to give you a very important task.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You give Kokomi's list of books to Gorou.

dialogues.speaker: Gorou
dialogues.text: Her Excellency's purchase list... Got it, this is how Her Excellency wants me to make up for my mistakes! No problem, just leave it to me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Gorou, let us come with you. We can show you around the Irodori Festival while we're at it.

dialogues.speaker: Gorou
dialogues.text: Thank you so much!

dialogues.speaker: Gorou
dialogues.text: There is a children's storybook on this list called "Night at Mt. Yougou." I think this is the stand where it's being sold.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A children's storybook?

dialogues.speaker: Gorou
dialogues.text: Yes. It's for the children of Watatsumi Island. Her Excellency says that this book is simply written and very useful for learning new words.

dialogues.speaker: Gorou
dialogues.text: Hello, I'll take five copies of "Night at Mt. Yougou," please.

dialogues.speaker: Fukumoto
dialogues.text: Thank you for your patronage!

dialogues.speaker: Fukumoto
dialogues.text: Wow, you're a lucky customer! There's a coupon in one of the books you just bought which entitles you to a free gift!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, Gorou got a free gift! That's amazing.

dialogues.speaker: Fukumoto
dialogues.text: Here you go — a toy fox, it's all yours!

dialogues.speaker: Gorou
dialogues.text: What? A—A toy fox?

dialogues.speaker: Fukumoto
dialogues.text: Are you okay? The hair on your tail is standing on end...

dialogues.speaker: Gorou
dialogues.text: I'm fine, thanks for the gift.

dialogues.speaker: Gorou
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, could you maybe, uh, look... l— look after the toy for me?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are you sure?

dialogues.speaker: Gorou
dialogues.text: Yes. As a thank-you gift for coming with me to buy the books.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *sigh* Seems like Gorou still hasn't recovered from seeing Miko.

dialogues.speaker: Gorou
dialogues.text: Okay, next up... Hmm, this isn't the focus of this trip, but let's go buy a light novel.

dialogues.speaker: Gorou
dialogues.text: It says on the list that Her Excellency had an editor called Onodera purchase the latest issue of "A Legend of Sword" for her in advance. We'd better not keep him waiting too long.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, we know him. We'll lead the way.

dialogues.speaker: Gorou
dialogues.text: Excuse me, are you Mr. Onodera? I'm here to pick up the new issue of "A Legend of Sword" for "Sole of the Deep."

dialogues.speaker: Onodera
dialogues.text: Hello there, yes, I have the book right here. I heard "Sole of the Deep" is a VIP of the Irodori Festival, but couldn't make it here in time for the signing event due to the shipping schedule.

dialogues.speaker: Gorou
dialogues.text: Also, if you have these books available, please give me one of each. Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Onodera
dialogues.text: Alright, let me see...

dialogues.speaker: Onodera
dialogues.text: Oh my goodness, it's your lucky day today, sir!

dialogues.speaker: Onodera
dialogues.text: You are the 100th reader to buy "The Saga of Hamavaran"! That entitles you to receive a special-edition version with a review personally written by Lady Yae herself!

dialogues.speaker: Gorou
dialogues.text: Ugh... are you serious?

dialogues.speaker: Onodera
dialogues.text: Are you okay? You don't look very well.

dialogues.speaker: Gorou
dialogues.text: I—I'm fine. Thank you for the books.

dialogues.speaker: Gorou
dialogues.text: Her Ex.... "Sole of the Deep" asked me to buy this book, after all. I'm sure she'll be very happy to receive a special version with a chief editor's review, hah, haha.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Gorou does not look like he's enjoying this at all. Paimon doesn't know if he's lucky or unlucky.

dialogues.speaker: Onodera
dialogues.text: Oh, one other thing — because of the amount of your purchase, you're able to enter the Yae Publishing House's lucky draw. Please come with me, right this way.

dialogues.speaker: Onodera
dialogues.text: Sir, please take your lucky draw whenever you are ready.

dialogues.speaker: Murata
dialogues.text: Just turn the handle and a prize ball will come out. Maybe today's your lucky day!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Come on, Gorou, go for it!

dialogues.speaker: Murata
dialogues.text: Let me see... Wow, incredible! You got the golden ball, that's the grand prize!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Gorou, you're a lucky dog today! So what is the grand prize, anyway?

dialogues.speaker: Murata
dialogues.text: The grand prize is a full collection of each light novel published by Yae Publishing House!

dialogues.speaker: Murata
dialogues.text: Not only is the prize awarded personally by Lady Yae, but you will also have the chance to shake hands and take a photo with her to commemorate the occasion!

dialogues.speaker: Gorou
dialogues.text: What? Not only do I have to meet her... but I have to shake her hand and take a photo with her, too!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Gorou! Hang in there!

dialogues.speaker: Youta
dialogues.text: What? This guy won the Yae Publishing House's grand prize? Wow, that's so lucky!

dialogues.speaker: Akito
dialogues.text: An entire set of all their light novels... That's worth a lot of money!

dialogues.speaker: Gorou
dialogues.text: Ugh... Um, excuse me, Ma'am, could we discuss this? I don't actually want the light novels.

dialogues.speaker: Murata
dialogues.text: Huh? You mean you want to give up the prize?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Gorou! Don't give up your prize! If you don't want to see Miko, that's fine — we'll figure something out!

dialogues.speaker: Gorou
dialogues.text: No, that's not what I meant. I'm not giving up the prize, and I can cope with the ceremony and the picture-taking.

dialogues.speaker: Gorou
dialogues.text: But I have a request. I would like to ask Yae Publishing House to change the prize from light novels to books on agricultural science of equivalent value.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Agricultural science?

dialogues.speaker: Gorou
dialogues.text: Yes. The land in Watatsumi Island is quite barren and always yields a poor grain harvest. We've been looking for new ways to improve the residents' lives.

dialogues.speaker: Gorou
dialogues.text: One of Her Ex... Sole of the Deep's core objectives for the Irodori Festival was to purchase some works on crop cultivation and aquaculture.

dialogues.speaker: Gorou
dialogues.text: If I can get these books as my prize instead, we can save a lot of money, and Sole of the Deep can buy some other useful resources, too.

dialogues.speaker: Murata
dialogues.text: I see. I understand your request, but I don't have the authority to grant it. Lady Yae will have to have the final say.

dialogues.speaker: Murata
dialogues.text: I will contact Lady Yae now — please wait for our reply at The Five Kasen Plaza. Depending on the situation, Lady Yae might need to negotiate this matter with you further in person.

dialogues.speaker: Gorou
dialogues.text: Okay, understood.

talks.objective: Wait at The Five Kasen Plaza
Wait at The Five Kasen Plaza

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Gorou, that was pretty brave of you. You clearly don't like having to deal with Miko, but you still agreed to the ceremony and even made your own demands.

dialogues.speaker: Gorou
dialogues.text: You think so? I guess I got a burst of courage when I thought about Her Excellency's orders and the people of Watatsumi Island.

dialogues.speaker: Gorou
dialogues.text: I am the general of Watatsumi Island's armed forces. How can I let something like this defeat me?

dialogues.speaker: Gorou
dialogues.text: I'm ready now. I feel like I'm back on the battlefield. Even if Yae Miko does come to negotiate with me, I won't let myself be pressured by her.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You still look pretty nervous, though, Gorou.

dialogues.speaker: Gorou
dialogues.text: Haha... well, probably because I just realized she might make a cunning counter-request just to toy with me.

dialogues.speaker: Murata
dialogues.text: Sorry for keeping you all waiting.

dialogues.speaker: Gorou
dialogues.text: How did it go? What did Guuji Yae say?

dialogues.speaker: Murata
dialogues.text: Lady Yae has agreed to your request to swap the light novels for books on agricultural science.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's great.

dialogues.speaker: Murata
dialogues.text: Additionally, Lady Yae says that she will include a few extra works, considering your intended use for those books.

dialogues.speaker: Murata
dialogues.text: You may accompany me to Yae Publishing House's warehouse to select your preferred books. I believe your return ship leaves tomorrow night? We will package the selected books and take them directly onto the ship for you.

dialogues.speaker: Gorou
dialogues.text: You'll package the books? Then, what about the ceremony?

dialogues.speaker: Murata
dialogues.text: Lady Yae said selecting the books may take up a lot of your time and energy. To ensure you have fond memories of the Irodori Festival, she decided to cancel the ceremony.

dialogues.speaker: Murata
dialogues.text: Although, she did leave you a letter. You can read it in your own time.

dialogues.speaker: Gorou
dialogues.text: I didn't think Yae Miko would cancel the ceremony. Huh, I was so convinced that she would try and make a fool out of me. Now it seems like I was overly suspicious of her.

dialogues.speaker: Gorou
dialogues.text: Anyway, I'll go with the editor to pick the books now. I won't trouble you guys anymore.

response.speaker: Gorou
response.text: Great. See you tomorrow night.

choices.text: We'll see you off at the harbor.

talks.objective: Go to the docks to see Kokomi and Gorou off (18:00 – 20:00 the next day)
Go to the docks to see Kokomi and Gorou off
Go to the docks to see Kokomi and Gorou off

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, thank you for coming to see us off.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How was your trip to Ritou?

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: Very worthwhile. The book review session was a big success, and I feel very positive about the forthcoming talks.

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: Gorou also made a great contribution. He procured a whole batch of useful books for Watatsumi Island.

dialogues.speaker: Gorou
dialogues.text: I may have won the prize, but ultimately it was Yae Miko who gave us all these books for free. If I have the chance in the future, I must thank her properly.

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: Speaking of, didn't Yae Miko send you a letter yesterday? What did it say?

dialogues.speaker: Gorou
dialogues.text: Oh, I almost forgot! I'll read it now...

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Dear Gorou, I suppose you must have been extremely nervous when you heard about the prospect of the award ceremony and the photo.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: It came as a surprise indeed to learn that not only did you accept those conditions, you also made your own demands. Your courage has won my respect.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Those books are a token of my goodwill to Watatsumi Island, and also my gift to you. I do hope you like them.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Ah yes, I'm sure that by this point you must be feeling ever so grateful for my kindness and are looking for a way to repay me, yes? Well, here's your chance.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Yae Publishing House will host an event next month, and we are looking for someone to dress up as a character from a light novel and interact with the fans.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Gorou, you are not only patient but also very beautiful. Why don't you come and help us? I'll prepare a tailor-made outfit, just for you.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Oh, and by the way — it'll be a woman's outfit.

dialogues.speaker: Gorou
dialogues.text: Aaaaah!!! I knew it, I knew she was up to something!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Kokomi and Gorou will be boarding their boat home soon. Let's go down to the harbor and see them off.
